solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Legal action over line in Bill’s article

indicators.note: one thing placed over another covers it on both sides, so the first piece wraps round the second

blocks.note: a cause is a case or lawsuit brought before a court
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is being brought about one line in a newspaper article written by someone called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: C(L)AUSE. 'Bill' looks like a person's name, but it is a parliamentary bill or contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is one numbered provision, or article, of a legislative bill or legal document.

clue.text: Include old politician in Conservative revolt

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces sits inside the later ones

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
Member of Parliament
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to rise up is to revolt

explanation.surface: A veteran MP is caught up in a Tory party rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolt' is not the definition but part of the wordplay; the old politician sits inside the Conservative uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprise is to contain or consist of, so a set comprises the things it includes.

clue.text: Everybody needs explicit permission to proceed

blocks.note: all means everybody
something explicit is clear and plainly stated

explanation.surface: Every person must receive express authorisation before going ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is a signal that danger has passed and it is safe to go on.

clue.text: Put up with removing tons of vomit

indicators.note: removing tells us to take something away from the word for putting up with

blocks.note: to stick something is to tolerate it
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates the job of clearing away huge quantities of vomit.
explanation.walkthrough: STICK loses its T to leave SICK. 'Tons of vomit' reads as a quantity, but 'of' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick is a colloquial noun for vomited matter, especially in British usage.

clue.text: Speak in Luxembourg about a form of transportation

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: Talk, while in Luxembourg, about some means of getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski-plane is an aircraft fitted with skis for landing on snow, so it is a mode of travel.

clue.text: Be acquainted with most of them before reckoning to be experienced

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter

blocks.note: to know someone is to be acquainted with them
taken as written, before trimming
a score is a tally or reckoning

explanation.surface: Getting to know people ahead of some settling of accounts makes one worldly.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOW + THE(m) + SCORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To know the score is an idiom for understanding how things really stand, being worldly-wise.

clue.text: What a hooker may do for change

blocks.note: first meaning: in rugby the hooker may throw or hand the ball to a teammate
second meaning: to turn or transform, as water may do into ice

explanation.surface: A sex worker's service in exchange for money.
explanation.walkthrough: The hooker is a rugby forward, not a prostitute; 'for change' suggests payment in coins but is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby player may pass the ball, and to pass into another state is to change.

clue.text: Determined after gunmen returned fire

indicators.note: returned means going back the way it came, so read the letters backwards

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
dour means stern and obstinately determined

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to act after armed men shot back.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery are the army's gunners; 'after' puts the determined word second.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate enthusiasm, and fire is used figuratively for the same intensity of feeling.

clue.text: Gallons on board before ship’s departure

indicators.note: something on board is carried inside the vessel

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
G is an abbreviation for gallons
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Fuel is loaded before a vessel sets sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a link word, but it is the vessel that the gallons board.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is a formal word for going out or leaving a place.

clue.text: Timid people assuming gangster’s evil intent

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so one piece takes in the other

blocks.note: timid people are called mice
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Fearful folk taking on a mobster's wicked purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: M(AL)ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to do harm, a wish to hurt others.

clue.text: Think about where footballers want to be in Costa Rica

indicators.note: one thing is inside another, so the second piece holds the first

blocks.note: CR is the international vehicle code for Costa Rica
attackers must be onside to avoid an offside flag

explanation.surface: A footballing question about a team's ambitions in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: C(ONSIDE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to ponder or reflect on it.

clue.text: Music case

blocks.note: first meaning: a piece played without singing
second meaning: a grammatical case expressing means, found in Russian and other languages

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a box for a violin; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece without vocals is an instrumental, and grammar names a case marking the means of an action the same way.

clue.text: Part of gold given back to the French

indicators.note: something given back travels in the opposite direction, so read it backwards

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Some of the gold has been returned to France.
explanation.walkthrough: OR reversed is RO, then LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is a part played by an actor in a film or play.

clue.text: A Native American set about returning home to make one

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for home is read backwards
placed around something, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a member of the Ute people
at home means in

explanation.surface: A tribesman is placed round the home he's coming back to.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ute are a Native American people of Utah and Colorado; at home means in.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together into a single whole.

clue.text: Potty starts to niff under the sink

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A child's toilet has begun to give off a smell under the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: A niff is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Potty and nuts are both informal words for crazy.

clue.text: Attempt to take in Lorca’s opening lines of praise

indicators.note: taking in means accepting inside, so one piece goes within another
an opening is a start, so only the initial letter is used

blocks.note: to have a go is to make an attempt
the initial of the Spanish poet's name
RY is short for railway lines

explanation.surface: An effort to absorb the first lines of a Lorca poem of tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: G(L)O + RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory is honour and acclaim, the praise given to God or to a hero.

clue.text: Try to persuade me to take time in retirement to exercise

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters go in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
physical training

explanation.surface: An appeal to a retired person to spend some time keeping fit.
explanation.walkthrough: ME plus T is turned round, then PT, the school abbreviation for physical training, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to entice or coax them into doing something.

clue.text: Cliff always felt fantastic before getting this disease

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wildly altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a scar is a steep rock face
the letters to rearrange
ever means always

explanation.surface: Cliff, perhaps Cliff Richard, said he always felt wonderful before catching an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff looks like a singer's name; a scar is a steep rock face. The rearranged letters sit in the middle, though 'always' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever is a bacterial infection marked by a red rash, so 'this disease' names it.

clue.text: Jack for instance resisted admitting about reporter’s source

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the other pieces go inside
'source' keeps only the first letter of 'reporter'

blocks.note: to face down an opponent is to resist
ca is short for circa, about
the opening letter of reporter

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack resisted letting a journalist's informant be revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: FACE(CA R)D. 'Jack' looks like a man's name; it is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is one of the court cards, alongside king and queen, which carry pictures of faces.

clue.text: City upset after failing to finish second is a case in point

indicators.note: failing to finish means the last letter is cut off
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters go in reverse

blocks.note: an instant is a second, a moment
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A city team in turmoil after not completing the match in second place.
explanation.walkthrough: INSTAN(t) followed by EC reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single example that illustrates a point.

clue.text: Mass murderer’s clothing likely to be rank

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a mass is a group or body
Cain killed Abel, the first murderer in the Bible
apt to means likely to

explanation.surface: A mass killer's outfit is probably foul-smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: GROUP + C(APT)AIN. 'Rank' looks like an adjective meaning smelly; it is a military grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Group captain is an RAF officer's rank, equivalent to an army colonel.

clue.text: Familiar with American editor at best falling short

indicators.note: falling short means not reaching the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: abbreviation for the United States
ED is short for editor
at its best is at the top

explanation.surface: A US editor who is, at best, not quite good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: US + ED + TO(p).
explanation.definitionFit: To be used to something is to be accustomed to it, which is being familiar with it.

clue.text: Not in appropriate clothes

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular noun: an outfit is a set of clothes

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: Someone is not wearing suitable attire.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' after 'Not' belongs to the wordplay, and the next 'in' is a link, though it reads like 'dressed in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of garments worn together.

clue.text: Check for nitrogen in advance

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a sub is an advance payment on wages
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Testing beforehand for nitrogen, like a chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: S(N)UB.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to rebuff them, checking their advances.

clue.text: Tried to find one amongst the rabble

indicators.note: amongst means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the herd is the common mass of people
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone tried to locate an individual within the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: HE(A)RD. 'Tried to find' suggests searching, but 'Tried' alone is the definition, in its courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who has heard a case has tried it in court.

clue.text: Support for some of Saussure’s theories

indicators.note: some of means just a part of the following words

blocks.note: found across the end of the name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Backing for some of the linguist Ferdinand de Saussure's ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest is a support or prop, as in an armrest or a cue rest in snooker.

clue.text: Girl edges away from drunk

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outer letters, which are taken off

blocks.note: tanked up, or tanked, means drunk

explanation.surface: A young woman slips away from an intoxicated man.
explanation.walkthrough: TANKED loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anke is a German and Dutch female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Opportunity arising for Othello perhaps

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means going upwards, so the letters read in reverse

blocks.note: room for manoeuvre is opportunity

explanation.surface: A chance coming up for an actor to play Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice, so he is one example.

clue.text: Sure to be wearing it after fellow’s swallowed by river

indicators.note: something swallowed is taken inside, so the earlier pieces go within
after places the word for fellow ahead of the word for wearing in the finished order

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
F is short for fellow
dressed in means wearing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone certain to be dressed in something after a man is carried off by the current.
explanation.walkthrough: The fellow comes first, then 'wearing it', and the river swallows all three; the Dee runs through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Definite means certain and settled, beyond doubt.

clue.text: Kill to acquire mother’s estate

indicators.note: acquiring something takes it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to do in is to kill
ma is mother, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A murder plot to grab one's mother's property.
explanation.walkthrough: DO(MA)IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is lands held by one owner, such as a lord's estate.

clue.text: They arrest a couple of Slavs after working under cover

indicators.note: a couple means two, so just the first pair of letters
to arrest someone is to hold them, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
taken as written
the opening two letters

explanation.surface: Police detain two Slavic people after an undercover operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' means the word for working goes first, even though it comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the sly means doing it secretly, unseen.

clue.text: Resentment shown by German character in Dickens

blocks.note: G is short for German
Barnaby Rudge, title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Bitterness displayed by a German figure in a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudge is lasting ill will held against someone for a past wrong.
